decisions.executionNote: Start right-arm elbow-up approach; coin is right of center, bank farther right. Raise and pitch before moving inward.
Continue raised right-hand approach toward the coin, keeping the left arm parked and rotating gradually toward a downward pinch.
Move over the holder at raised clearance, adjusting yaw to the coin's visible slant. Recheck alignment before descent.
Bring right wrist directly above the holder with open jaws, continuing gradual downward orientation while maintaining elbow-up continuity.
Complete downward pinch orientation and center over the coin. Keep jaws open while visually checking the holder alignment.
Use wrist view to move left toward the coin center and descend 15 mm with jaws open; holder remains clear.
Coin is between the open fingers at grasp depth. Fine-center and remove small yaw error while closing gradually around its faces.
Fully close and let fingers settle, then test retention with a small vertical lift; judge coin motion in the wrist view.
Lift straight above the holder with the right gripper fully closed. Verify separation and retention before transporting to the bank.
Coin looks tilted at the fingertips; pause then make a small raised transfer to verify it travels with the closed gripper.
Coin did not stay with the fingers and is beside the holder. Reopen and approach its new visible position for a deeper, centered grasp.
Coin has settled flat beside the holder. Lower the open downward gripper toward the rim, then recenter at table-level grasp height.
Center the flat coin between the jaws and approach its rim just above the tabletop; begin closing gradually without sweeping the coin.
Hold the centered rim-level pose and close the right fingers around the flat coin, allowing time for closure before another lift.
Test the new rim grasp with a slow vertical lift, keeping the right gripper fully closed and monitoring the coin relative to the fingers.
Continue vertical lift past 8 cm while keeping the coin clamped. The coin is mostly obscured between the jaws; check retention before lateral motion.
Coin is still on the table, not retained. Reopen and recenter over its visible new location, approaching lower for a rim grasp.
Refine the flat-coin alignment from the wrist image while lowering open jaws; aim to surround its rim rather than close above it.
Center the disk laterally and lower another centimeter to engage the rim near table height, then begin a gentle closure.
Descent is limited by tabletop contact. Hold this height and close slowly on the centered coin rim without further downward motion.
Settle the rim pinch and make a 9 mm test lift, watching whether the disk remains between the jaw ends.
The disk escaped sideways. Reopen, recenter over its new position and lower the jaw ends a few millimeters closer to its thin rim.
Level the two jaw ends so both reach the thin coin rim evenly, compensating the wrist translation to avoid sweeping the disk.
Recenter the disk slightly farther inside the jaw tips and lower by only 2 mm, closing partway for a symmetric rim pinch.
Move the coin deeper between the flat inner jaw surfaces rather than gripping only at the pointed ends; keep table height unchanged.
Finish closing symmetrically on the deeper-positioned rim and allow the pinch to settle before lifting.
Slow 15 mm lift to test whether the deeper rim pinch retains the disk, with no lateral motion.
Check retention while slightly pitching the fingertips forward at raised clearance. If the disk remains on the table, use a tip-first angled approach instead of another flat pinch.
The disk is visible near the tips after pitching. Lift vertically another 4 cm with the jaws closed to distinguish retention from a table-level disk.
The coin remained on the tabletop. Reopen and use a more oblique tip-first approach to engage the thin rim rather than close above it.
Lower the open oblique jaws toward the disk, adjusting forward alignment from the head and wrist views while preserving the same elbow configuration.
Fine-align the oblique fingertips with the disk's near rim and lower carefully while partly closing. Stop further descent if tracking indicates table contact.
Table contact limits depth; hold observed height, center the rim laterally, and close the oblique jaws without pressing farther down.
The oblique jaw ends contact opposite sides of the rim. Maintain full closure, settle, and test with a 9 mm vertical lift.
The disk now stays fixed between the jaw tips during lift. Raise vertically above 8 cm while maintaining full closure.
Retention is visible. Raise and move toward the bank while slowly reorienting the rim-held coin toward a vertical insertion plane; keep the left arm parked.
Continue the raised transfer within the right workspace and rotate gradually; the coin remains visibly seated between the fingertips.
Carry the retained coin toward the bank at clearance height, continuing gradual rotation toward the slot's vertical plane.
Maintain the stable rim grasp and clearance while translating rightward and continuing the slow insertion-plane rotation.
Approach above the slot while finishing the controlled rotation of the retained disk. Keep clearance and preserve elbow-up continuity.
Continuity guard stopped the far-side approach. Retreat slightly toward the robot and unwind the wrist in small increments while retaining the coin.
Bridge between the observed pose and the last accepted target, then settle. Avoid adding a new large joint change after the guard interruption.
Unwind away from the wrist limit with very small retreat increments. Coin has shifted at the tips, so preserve closure and avoid abrupt motion.
Coin has slipped beside the bank. Open and withdraw at clearance while unwinding the wrist, then reacquire its settled position from RGB.
Approach the coin's new tabletop location beside the bank at reduced height, finishing the wrist unwind while keeping the jaws open.
Open fingers were close to the bank. Narrow to a safe pregrasp opening and approach the coin from its clear left side with oblique fingertips.
Move away from the bank toward the visible coin before further descent; finish the oblique approach with a compact jaw opening.
Descend toward the visible disk with the oblique gripper clear of the bank, keeping a compact opening and correcting lateral alignment.
The bank is obstructing descent. Lift clear and turn the compact gripper toward an approach from behind the disk rather than press into the bank.
Lower the compact oblique gripper toward the centered disk from the clearer side, monitoring clearance from the bank.
Descent is obstructed by the bank-side finger. Lift clear and turn around the coin to approach from behind with the jaws closing across, not toward, the bank.
Continue the compact arc behind the coin, lowering only as the bank-side finger clears. Maintain elbow-up and small joint-continuous increments.
Replan from the interrupted pose: stop the rearward arc and lower in small vertical increments at the current clear, compact orientation.
Lower toward rim height and correct the disk's small lateral offset. Keep the compact open fingers clear of the bank.
Engage the centered rim with the oblique tips, lower the last few millimeters, then close without further descent.
Test the rim contact with a slow 12 mm lift. The disk shifted during closure, so verify retention before any transfer.
The coin stayed on the table. Reopen, center its shifted rim, and level the jaw ends before lowering for symmetric contact.
Close on the centered disk with leveled oblique jaw ends; keep the pose stationary as the rim pinch settles.
The jaws passed above the rim. Reopen and adjust the tip-first pitch and depth by a few millimeters to contact the coin edge symmetrically.
Finish the centered oblique rim pinch, then test retention with an 8 mm vertical lift before committing to transport.
The tips closed above the rim. Reopen, lower a few millimeters and place the disk slightly deeper between the leveled oblique jaws.
Finish the low rim pinch, settle fully closed, and make a very small lift to check whether the disk is captured.
